newsitem.title: LEBANON: Most active Beirut shares up on week.
newsitem.headline: Most active Beirut shares up on week.

text.p: Most of the active stocks on the Beirut Stock Exchange rose in the week ended on Thursday despite sharply reduced turnover and dealers said a slow upward trend would continue next week.
The BLOM stock index rose 1.07 percent and the LISPI share index rose 1.35 percent to 84.46. The LIBX bank index rose 0.33 on the week to 118.48.
Markets and financial markets are closed on Friday for the Good Friday holiday.
Banque Audi rose on the week, Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce was steady, Solidere A and B went up and two industrial shares were mixed.
"It was a busy week. There was demand on all six shares. Most prices went up slowly. I expect similar trading next week," a dealer said.
Audi rose to $19.125 from last Friday's $19 on turnover of 71,348 from 82,549.
The other listed bank, Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce, held steady at $13.625 on sharply reduced turnover of 19,284 shares from 61,831 last week.

The market is awaiting the imminent listing of a third bank, Bank of Beirut, which said on Tuesday that its $10 million private share placement prior to listing attracted applications for shares worth $90 million.
Listing of 30 percent of Bank of Beirut's shares is expected within two weeks.
Solidere A shares rose to $10.375 from $10.25 and Solidere B rose to $10.875 from $10.75.
A total of 543,454 Solidere shares were traded compared with 1,084,283 a week earlier.
"The fact that the huge oversupply problem of A shares in previous weeks was over relaxed the market and activated it. It opened the door for new opportunities," the dealer said.
Ciments Libanais, which rose on Wednesday to $1.21875, fell back on Thursday to last week's $1.1875 on a turnover of 4,500 shares from last week's 5,500.
Eternit rose to $1.875, from $1.6875 at their previous trade on March 13. Turnover was 7,250 shares, up from zero last week.
There was no trade in the two other listed firms throughout the week: Uniceramic and Ciments Blancs.
Total weekly turnover fell to 645,836 from 1,319,707 and value was $7,277,705 against $13,730,125.
